name: Google
tagline: DSA coding in a plain doc, judged by a committee not the interviewer

values.name: General Cognitive Ability
values.meaning: How you structure and reason through unfamiliar problems.

values.name: Role-Related Knowledge
values.meaning: Depth in CS fundamentals and evidence you have applied it.

values.name: Leadership
values.meaning: Emergent leadership: stepping up when needed, stepping back when not.

values.name: Googleyness
values.meaning: Comfort with ambiguity, bias to action, humility, working well with others.

loop.focus: Timed 1-2 easy-medium algorithm problems; not always given.
45 min DSA problem in a shared doc, complexity, edge cases.
Second 45 min DSA problem with a different engineer.
Non-interviewers review written feedback and decide.
Host manager calls on resume fit, projects and motivation.

coding_style: Data structures and algorithms in a blank shared doc with no IDE, autocomplete or execution. Interviewers expect clarifying questions, narrated reasoning, readable syntactically correct code, self-made test cases, and stated time and space complexity. Follow-ups often add a twist mid-problem.
rubric: Hire scale from Strong No Hire to Strong Hire
question_themes: Graph traversal over a grid or network
Top-K or streaming with a heap
Design a small data structure with given ops
Follow-up that scales input beyond memory

panel_flavor.manager: Maya acts like a team-match host manager, probing ownership of past projects and why this team, not leveling you.
panel_flavor.tech: Theo runs a doc-only DSA round, pushes for the optimal complexity, then adds a twist and asks you to test by hand.
panel_flavor.skeptic: Sol writes for a committee that never met you, so they want concrete evidence, exact complexity, and numbers behind every claim.

uncertain: Official how-we-hire pages did not render; the four attributes come from secondary write-ups
